Dollar cost averaging means investing a fixed amount on a schedule, for example every month from each salary, instead of trying to time the market. When prices are low the same amount buys more shares, when prices are high it buys fewer. Statistically a lump sum invested at once usually does slightly better because markets rise more often than they fall, but regular investing removes the temptation to wait for a dip that never comes. It works best with broad [[Index funds]].
